Unprivileged belligerents comes from the Geneva Convention.

"BUT WHAT'S ILL INTENT!? THEY'LL JUST HOLD THEM IF THEY WANT TO PAINT THE US IN A NEGATIVE LIGHT!"

A journalist is more than welcome to talk shit about the US or its troops. Even the article makes it clear that this does not give commanders free reign to banish journalists that are hurting their feelings.

A journalist is not, however, allowed to feed NATO grid-coordinates to enemy combatants, poison the water supply on a remote base, steal grenades from ammunition depots etc. These things have happened in wars throughout all of history. It's espionage. Spying. Of course we have to establish laws and rules on the subject.

But the point is that this power can be misused. It is one thing to say that you have evidence that someone has committed espionage and should be arrested or detained, but it is another to simply label someone as a "belligerent" and then detain them when you have no evidence of any wrongdoing at all other than having someone speak their mind. In this way, you can label anyone that speaks out against a despotic regime for example as a belligerent and detain them even though they have done nothing but express an unpopular opinion. This was the whole reason why there was outrage about the NDAA to begin with, and codifying it in law isn't going to make the situation any better. All it takes it one tyrant to take power, and this will provide the tool to silence the entire media, and more importantly, all dissenting point of views.

We do our best to mitigate these issues. To think it would be easy for an officer to get away with this is misguided, especially in today's playing field. I guarantee you that the detaining of a journalist would be met with an extreme level of scrutiny. It would be career ending for any commander to abuse this power.
